paragraphs.text: In Magic , species is a subset of the characteristic " creature type ". Until 2025, this was designated as race .

Originally "Race" designated the unique genetic makeup of a sapient (and usually humanoid) creature group. Besides race, most Magic cards with humanoid creatures may also have another creature type : the class represents their career or calling in life. This is known as the species/class model .

Note that the the original Magic approach was somewhat different from the scientific one. In biology, the basic unit of biological classification and taxonomic rank is " species ", which is defined as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offspring. Race in that aspect is defined as a genetically distinct population of individuals within the same species. It is also worth noting that the Wizards of the Coast 's owned IP Dungeons & Dragons replaced "race" with "species" in 2024.
Hybrid species or cards depicting multiple characters sometimes have multiple species types. There are currently 96 cards with multiple species types.
In March 2025, Mark Rosewater revealed that R&D had started using "species" for Magic as well.

paragraphs.text: Some acorn sets, like Unglued , Unhinged , and Unstable , use creature types which are not included in Magic's comprehensive rules , but are part of 'silver-border' games. Because these creature types are not compiled into an authoritative list by Wizards of the Coast, the following table may be incomplete and which silver-border creature types are considered species and non-species is currently based on intuition rather than official comment.
